question.problem:
Calculate the radius of a sphere given that its surface area is $50\pi \: \textrm{cm}^2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252847/assets/99bb0ea67859fbd109442fcf698427ea43452087b4523b7202a760a2a8b27052.png)
question.worked_solution:
We can calculate the surface area of a sphere using the formula

$$
S = 4 \pi r^2,
$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $S=50\pi \: \textrm{cm}^2$ into the formula, we can solve for $r$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\ 50\pi  & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\ \frac{50\pi }{4\pi } & ={r}^{2} \\ {r}^{2} & =\frac{25}{2} \\ r & =\sqrt{\frac{25}{2}} \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}
$$
